statement: Three natural numbers greater than or equal to 2 are written (not necessarily distinct), and from them a sequence is constructed by the following rule: if the second-to-last number written is \(a\), the one before it is \(b\), and the last is \(c\), then the next term \(x\) satisfies \(x \cdot c = a + b + 186\). Determine all possible initial triples such that when the process continues indefinitely all the terms generated are natural numbers greater than or equal to 2.

Let \(C_1\) and \(C_2\) be two circles externally tangent to each other, with centers \(O_1\) and \(O_2\) respectively. From \(O_1\), the two tangent lines to \(C_2\) are drawn, intersecting \(C_1\) at \(P\) and \(P'\). From \(O_2\), the two tangent lines to \(C_1\) are drawn, intersecting \(C_2\) at \(Q\) and \(Q'\). Prove that segment \(PP'\) equals segment \(QQ'\).

In a trick card tournament, \(2k\) people sign up. All possible matches are played, with the condition that in each match each of the four players knows his partner and does not know either of his two opponents. Determine the maximum number of matches that can be played in such a tournament.
Coins of diameter 1 have been placed on a square of side 11, without overlapping or protruding from the square. Can there be 126 coins? And 127? And 128?

A rectangular puzzle is assembled with 2000 pieces that are all equal rectangles, similar to the large rectangle, with sides parallel to those of the large one. The shortest side of each piece measures 1. Determine the minimum possible value of the area of the large rectangle.

Consider the set \(E\) of all fractions \(\tfrac{1}{n}\), where \(n\) is a natural number. A maximal arithmetic progression of length \(k\) in \(E\) is an arithmetic progression of \(k\) terms, all belonging to \(E\), that cannot be extended to the left or to the right with another element of \(E\).

For example, \(\tfrac{1}{20}, \tfrac{1}{8}, \tfrac{1}{5}\) is a maximal arithmetic progression of length 3 in \(E\).

Prove that for every integer \(k > 2\), there exists a maximal arithmetic progression of length \(k\) in \(E\).
